'''''Hypericum pulchrum''''' is a [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Hypericaceae]], commonly known as '''slender St John's-wort'''.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> It is native to Western Europe.

==Description==
''Hypericum pulchrum'' is a dainty, [[Rhizome|rhizomatous]] [[perennial]] plant growing {{convert|9-18|in|cm|abbr=on}} high. It has erect smooth stems without ridges or wings. It has a few opposite pairs of untoothed, heart-shaped leaves that half clasp the stem. They are dotted with transparent spots and often have inrolled margins. The terminal [[inflorescence]] has rich yellow flowers. Each of these has five small, broad, blunt sepals with black dots on the margins. The five petals are red beneath and have red and black dots on the margins. There are three styles and many [[stamen]]s with orange anthers in three bundles. The fruit is a [[Dehiscence (botany)|dehiscent]] [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]].<ref name=PGWF>McKlintock, D. and R. S. R. Fitter. The Pocket Guide to Wild Flowers. (1956) Collins, London. P28.</ref><ref name=Skye>[http://www.plant-identification.co.uk/skye/guttiferae/hypericum-pulchrum.htm Slender St John's Wort] West Highland Flora. Retrieved 2011-09-14.</ref>

==Habitat==
''Hypericum pulchrum'' is a [[calcifuge]], found in heathy places, dry moorlands, among rocks in upland regions and on road verges on non-calcareous soils.<ref name=BSBI>{{cite web | title=Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora: ''Hypericum pulchrum'' |url=https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/hypericum-pulchrum |publisher=Botanical Society of Britain and Ireland |access-date=14 May 2018 }}</ref><ref name=Skye/><ref name=Bwf>[http://www.ukwildflowers.com/Web_pages/hypericum_pulchrum_slender_st_johns_wort.htm ''Hypericum pulchrum'': Slender St. John's-wort] British wild flowers. Retrieved 2011-09-14.</ref>

==Distribution==
''Hypericum pulchrum'' is found growing in Austria, Belgium, Britain, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain, Sweden and Switzerland.<ref>[http://rbg-web2.rbge.org.uk/cgi-bin/nph-readbtree.pl/feout?FAMILY_XREF=&GENUS_XREF=Hypericum&SPECIES_XREF=pulchrum&TAXON_NAME_XREF=&RANK= ''Hypericum pulchrum''] Flora Europaea. Retrieved 2009-09-15.</ref> It is found in suitable habitats throughout the United Kingdom.<ref name=Bwf/> It has been introduced to [[New Zealand]] where it has spread across the South Island and the southern part of the North Island.<ref>[http://www.nzflora.info/factsheet/Taxon/Hypericum_pulchrum.html ''Hypericum pulchrum'' L.] Flora of New Zealand. Retrieved 2011-09-14.</ref>
